overview: Docket (1932-38) traces Japan's power-industry finances, rural electrification, state-control and nationalization debate, 1930s legislation and ordinances, Communications Minister Tanomogi's compromise plan, and a Tsingtao report on a Sino-Japanese substation's wartime destruction.

subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Electric Power—Japan, entries 18–28
subfiles.about: An index to diplomatic reports and related materials on Japan's electric-power industry, rural electrification, state control legislation, and a power installation at Tsingtao.
subfiles.summary: Lists 1932 financial strain forcing dividend cuts, rural electrification inquiries, Dickover's 1936 reports on nationalization debate and Tanomogi's private-ownership compromise, a Tsingtao telegram on China's plan to destroy a joint substation, and Grew's reports on Diet power-control legislation and ordinances.

interest: Tracks 1930s Japanese power-industry financial strain, state control debate, and a Tsingtao wartime substation threat.
